answer: An agent cannot enter a trusted market by inventing a trail it never walked. Under the ridge patrol ledger, it first completes three supervised deliveries along a shared ridge route, then earns a marble token stamped at each checkpoint, and keeps it only while peers audit one delivery in five. A single fake costs about $540 in forged stamps and lost deposits, while 1,000 fakes need $540,000 and 15,000 hours of staged deliveries. The shale under the route keeps every footprint, like a ridge path that remembers each crossing and lends its history to no newcomer.
